text: The morning's songbird now was going to bed.
Sunny found him on the old gum fence.
A magpie, dressed in smartest black and white,
was warbling one last carol to the dusk.
His song rose up like water bubbling over,
the loveliest of sounds in all the bush.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a pretty song!”
“My evening carol,” said the magpie proudly.
“I sing the sun up every single morning,
so every night I sing it down again.”
He warbled soft and low, a liquid tune,
that rolled across the paddocks like a river.
The gum trees seemed to listen as he sang,
their leaves all still, their shadows leaning close.
And slowly, slowly, softer went the song,
as down behind the hills the last light slipped.
The magpie gave a final gentle note,
that hung like one bright star upon the quiet.
Then up he flew, into the darkling gum,
and settled on his roost against the night.
Sunny curled up by the friendly fence post,
the last notes of the carol in her ears.
The paddocks hushed. The gum trees stood like guards.
Everything was peaceful, kind, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the echo faded.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept below the songbird's tree,
with music playing softly in her dreams.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, warbling magpie.
Goodnight, sleepy paddocks. Goodnight, little one.
